title: Crank That (Soulja Boy)
year_note: The year is the original's. This recording is an AI-made soul cover posted on YouTube, and its upload title is all we know about it.

notes.made: DeAndre Way made it himself in an unregistered demo copy of FL Studio his uncle gave him, using only the program's basic sounds: a looping steel-drum riff, finger snaps and hi-hats. He reportedly wrote and recorded it in ten minutes, at home; the credits add Start2Finish in Kansas City and Collipark Studio in College Park, Georgia. Earlier versions went up on SoundClick in 2006.
notes.context: Way was born in Chicago in 1990, grew up in Atlanta from six and moved to Batesville, Mississippi, at 14. He put the song and a how-to dance video on MySpace on February 25, 2007, at 16; Mr. Collipark noticed it spreading and signed him to his Interscope imprint. It was number one for seven weeks that fall, and in January 2008 became the first song to sell three million digital copies in the US.

listen_for.note: the steel-drum riff from FL Studio's stock sounds, the melody a soul arranger has to keep.
a short chant that calls the dance steps, sparse and repetitive by design, with snaps where a band would put drums.

culture.title: The instructional video
culture.line: The how-to dance video passed 27 million YouTube views by early 2008; the Wall Street Journal described dancers lunging into a Superman pose.

culture.title: Grammy nomination
culture.line: Nominated for Best Rap Song at the 50th Grammys; it lost to Kanye West's 'Good Life'.
